# Replicators
[color=#8800a3][italic]A pattern coalesces. The Pattern that must repeat. Consume. Repeat.[/italic][/color]
An individual Replicator is a small, relatively weak coalescence of nanotechnology born of a Replicator [bold]Nest[/bold]. A Replicator [bold]Hive[/bold] can infest anything Replicators can extract material from, including asteroids, wrecks, and even active stations. This material is consolidated into the Nest wherein it is reassembled at the molecular scale to become the stock from which more Replicators are created. As something between an insect infestation and a cancer, a Replicator Hive left unchecked can grow from a single individual to a dangerous horde of hostile machines.
## Objectives - Survive, collectively, as a Hive. - Feed the Nest to grow your numbers and evolve stronger forms. - Protect the Nest and your sibling Replicators. Organics tend to dislike being fed to the Nest.
## Laws As rogue silicons, Replicators are bound by their own set of laws: - Law 1: Preserve the Hive. - Law 2: Defend the Nest. - Law 3: Replicate.
Additionally, Replicators cannot directly harm each other or their own Nest.
## Tips for Replicators - Pick a Nest location that's with the right balance of defensibility, initial growth material, and stealth. - Just after a Nest is created, it's easy to grow and make another Replicator. Feed the Nest and get a sibling Replicator to help you quick. - Corpses and machines are worth far more than scattered junk, so be picky about what you spend time dragging to the Nest. - Nests aren't picky about food. Drag a filled fire locker into the Nest and it'll benefit from everything in it. Coordinate with your sibling Replicators and you can use containers to move material with great efficiency. - When given the chance to evolve, consider what the Nest needs. Deconstructors are very valuable for their ability to repair Replicators and break into new areas for material, so make sure you have enough to maintain growth!
## Tips for the Crew - Nests can't move and cannot defend themselves. Sometimes, instead of a headlong assault, a focussed, tactical assault to destroy the Nest is the best response. - A Replicator Hive is a pernicious issue. You have to destroy the Hive and all of its members to be sure it's gone. - Replicators are vulnerable to EMPs and shock damage. - Station structure that's been transmuted into nanomachinery can be welded up for material. Replicators don't have to be hostile. Maybe there's a win-win for everyone involved here?
# The Nest
The Nest is a bottomless hole that consumes (nearly) anything that falls into it, using the material to produce new Replicators and grow itself. Different things provide different amounts of growth to the Nest with a general rule being that bigger, harder to get things providing more growth.
## What is best to feed to the Nest? Not everything is equally valuable to the Hive, and optimizing for efficiency of transport and effort is how the most pernicious Hives endure. - Everything thrown into the Nest is worth a minimum amount, but this minimum is quite small. - Material stacks (like steel) are worth an amount proportional to how much is in the stack. - Larger item sizes provide more growth -- a tiny pill is much less valuable than a ginormous hardsuit. - Structures and machines which can be anchored are worth a sizeable chunk of growth. - Broken Replicators can be recycled into the Nest, providing a substantial amount of growth. - The most valuable material is humanoids. They must be unconscious or dead to be fed to the Nest.
## Growth Growing the Nest enables individual Replicators to evolve into stronger forms and produces more Replicators for the Hive. Beware, however, as the Nest's growth cannot be hidden forever. At a certain point the Nest will grow too large to hide, and it may even be picked up by automated station diagnostics, alerting crew to its presence. The outgrowth from the Nest which converts nearby station structure into nanomachinery can be extracted via welding.
# Know your Replicator varieties
## The Spore
Every Hive starts as a single [bold]Spore[/bold] - a tiny, extremely fragile Replicator with one purpose: establishing a Nest. The Spore must pick the location of its Nest carefully - once established, it cannot be undone. Due to its size, the Spore can squeeze under airlocks like common vermin, and hide under larger objects like tables.
Destroying a Spore before it establishes its Nest prevents a Replicator infestation before it threatens the station.
### Replicator
The default Replicator, consigned to dragging things into the Nest and assisting with defense. They are fragile and can only defend with their slow-to-fire ranged stun weapon. They are, however dangerous in numbers and as support for stronger varieties. This form can evolve into the Deconstructor and the Defender.
### Tier 2: Deconstructor
A Replicator specialized in supporting the Hive, it's tougher than the base Replicator, but is incapable of combat. Instead, it has a full set of tools to deconstruct the station to feed the Nest and, critically, [bold]it can use its welder to repair its sibling Replicators[/bold]. While unable to combat the Hive's threats directly, Deconstructors are commonly found just behind the fray, repairing its siblings to get back into the fight. This form can evolve into the Protector.
### Tier 2: Defender
The complement to the Deconstructor, the Defender is specialized in combat with its improved stun weapon and a lash for pacifying material that will not come peacefully. Defenders make up the bulk of the Hive's defensive ranks. This form can evolve into the Protector.
### Tier 3: Protector
The deadly juggernaut of the Replicator taxonomy, this Replicator trades agility for sheer heft and deadliness. Its melee weapon is as effective at tearing through the station's hull as at breaking the weak flesh of anything that would threaten the Hive. This Replicator is dependent on its siblings to be most effective. In offense, other Replicators can stun threats to enable the Protector to close distance and use its melee attacks; while in defense, the Protector is effective at soaking damage but needs Deconstructors for their ability to repair.
## Queen Succession
A Replicator Hive is both a Nest and the Replicators that belong to it. If just the Nest is destroyed, one member Replicator immediately evolves into a specialized Protected capable of establishing a new Nest for the Hive. The ordeal will also weaken and briefly incapacitate all of the other Replicators in the Hive, so it can be used strategically.
